what: A blurred aurora wave flows slowly inside a round window in the middle (darkening from .22~.85 at the edge) on a fixed canvas behind the page (flow .018 · rotation .04 rad/s · twist .41). Once the top edge of the storm Section passes 60% of the screen, the same wave crosses over into a vortex (twist 3.6 · radius .6→.86 · blur .5→.66 · rotation .22 rad/s · flow .045 · brightness 1.35) at a rate of 1.8 per second, and past 28% of the Section’s progress it returns to calm. While the top edge of the warm tail passes 90%→15% of the screen, the five colors shift to warm partners with twist .2 · brightness 1.8 (max .5 per second). Drawn at .55x screen resolution (WebGL)

options.storm: CSS selector of the long section to turn into a swirl — if absent, it stays calm
options.reach: storm: up to what section progress the swirl is kept, default .28
options.warm: CSS selector of the tail that changes color on approach
options.look: With local, it is laid only inside this element rather than fixed to the screen
options.--fx-aurora-bg|deep|mid|glow|bright: Five colors at rest (via style) — default is a mix of the background and accent colors
options.--fx-aurora-warm-*: Five colors as the tail approaches (via style) — default leans toward tints of the accent color

from.where: shared.js #aurora-bg — aurora behind every page, swirls at the home page brain section (.a-brain), turns green at the footer

note: The original shader is simplex noise. Ours is a rewrite using value noise stretched to -1.2~1.2, with the same number of steps (3 layers · 2 warps · 3-direction blur)
